title: The overhead foot pedal and Dave Biddy's drums
summary: He describes the old overhead foot pedal with rod and spring, and Dave Biddy as the last man to own one.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Were there any of the numbers that, I think the music, that is, the dance music, sound anything like the jazz today, that is, to have the same kind of a beat? Well, I'll tell you. What was your say?

Well, the beat was much different from the day on the ottoman for the drums that we had and the foot pellet was different. Now we had what you call an overhead foot pattern. Yeah. That foot pellet would come over and it had a rod and a spring in the middle and it would kick out on the back. And that drummer would hit arm where he had to raise up his foot for the foot to let back. And for the get the pressure where that spring would pull it and release it.
I've heard I never did see one.
Well, the overhead, well, Dave Biddy had one and I told him not to get rid of it. Because he played with me during the war. He was the last man to have one of those.

Yeah, Dave Biddy. Overhead foot pattern. And people would look at that thing. They'd never seen one. And then you could hit in the drum with it and hit that double time in there with your stick. Oh, I see.
But now I said they put the ludric, well, that drummer don't hit like that because the ludric is more faster. But they used to hit that drum and then they hit in there with that stick.
Yeah, that's right. The drum stick. Get them double beats. But he had that overhead foot pedal on there. Yeah. And it sounded nice. It kept time. It sounded nice.
